Proton creates a contact for everyone you exchange email with, so your phone fills with entries you never added. Rules let you decide which contacts reach this phone. They are checked in order and the first one that matches decides, so the order matters. Anything no rule matches is handled by the setting at the bottom of the list. Contacts are never deleted from your Proton account: a rule only stops them being copied here, and you are always asked before anything is removed from the phone.

Sets the language used for this app\'s own screens. \"Auto\" follows your phone\'s system language. This only changes the app interface, it does not translate your synced calendar events or contacts.

The name shown for this account in Android Settings → Accounts and in calendar/contact app pickers. It\'s only a local label; changing it does not affect your Proton account.\n\nNote: Samsung Calendar and Samsung Contacts ignore custom account names and always show their own label (e.g. \"Proton\"). Your chosen name may not appear there, this is a Samsung limitation we can\'t change. Other apps (Google Calendar/Contacts) show it normally.

How often the app checks Proton in the background for remote changes to your contacts and calendar. Shorter intervals surface changes faster but use more battery and data. This is separate from manual sync, which you can trigger any time with the sync buttons.

Shows a silent, ongoing notification while a sync runs, with live progress (scanning, downloading, decrypting). It sits at the bottom of the notification shade and never makes a sound. Turn it off if you\'d rather sync run invisibly.

When on, your Proton contacts sync two-way with Android\'s contacts: changes on either side are merged.\n\nNote: Samsung Contacts shows contacts under a single \"Proton contacts\" account label and hides the email subtitle for third-party accounts like ours, a hard-coded Samsung limitation we can\'t change. Google Contacts and most other apps display them normally.

How often the app does a complete re-check instead of a fast incremental sync. A full sync catches anything an incremental pass might miss (e.g. changes made while offline) at the cost of more time and data. Leave at the default unless you suspect items aren\'t syncing.

Shows a notification if a sync fails (e.g. network error or expired session). Tap it for a plain-language reason and a link to the logs. Turn it off if you don\'t want to be alerted about transient failures.

When on, your Proton calendars sync into Android\'s calendar, so events appear in Google Calendar, Samsung Calendar and any other calendar app. Two-way: edits you make on the phone upload back to Proton for calendars you own.

Proton can hold subscribed calendars (e.g. an external ICS feed) and holiday calendars. These are read-only on Proton\'s side. When off, the app skips them and syncs only your own editable calendars. Turn on if you also want those read-only calendars mirrored to your phone.

\"All events\" syncs your entire calendar history and all future events, best if you want everything on your phone (the first sync of a large calendar can take several minutes). \"Custom range\" syncs only a window of days around today, keeping large calendars fast and light. Events outside the window aren\'t downloaded.
How many days before and after today to sync when \"Custom range\" is selected. Larger windows show more of your calendar but take longer to sync. Has no effect in \"All events\" mode.

When on, the app periodically re-checks events that have attendees to detect accept/decline/tentative responses. Proton\'s change feed doesn\'t report RSVP changes, so this needs extra API calls, only worth enabling if you rely on seeing attendees\' responses on your phone.
When you add attendees to an event on your phone, email them an invitation. Off by default: turn on only if you want the app to email participants on your behalf.
Email attendees when you change the details (time, location, etc.) of an event they\'re invited to. Off by default.
Email attendees when you delete an event they\'re invited to, so their calendars remove it too. Off by default.

When sending invitation emails, put the event\'s title in the email subject line so recipients recognize it at a glance. Off by default for privacy: email subjects aren\'t encrypted in standard mail transport, so the title would be visible to mail servers along the route.

Android may pause background sync to save battery, which can delay or stop automatic syncing. Excluding this app from battery optimization keeps scheduled syncs running reliably. Use the button to open the system battery settings for the app.

Captures extra diagnostic detail (auth state, key unlock, sync internals) in the log, helpful when reporting a problem. It may include account email addresses and calendar names, so only share logs with the developer. Leave off for normal use.

Writes the app log to a timestamped text file (sync-for-proton-log-….txt) in a folder you choose. The app otherwise keeps its log in memory only, so turn this on to capture a problem that is hard to reproduce. A new file is created each time the app starts; it may contain account email addresses and calendar names, so only share it with the developer. Leave off for normal use.

Event times depend on time zone rules, and countries change these rules from time to time. Android keeps them in the phone's time zone data, which arrives with system updates. A phone that no longer gets them, for example an older Android version or a phone without Google Play system updates, keeps the old rules, and events in places whose rules have changed since then can show at the wrong time.

Time zone data on this phone: version %1$s

When off (the default), the app uses the phone's own time zone data and sends nothing to www.tzurl.org.

When on, the app downloads the current rules for each time zone your events use from www.tzurl.org, a third-party service, at most once per time zone each time the app starts, and uses them only if they are newer than the phone's own. www.tzurl.org then sees your IP address and the names of those time zones, for example Europe/Berlin. Nothing else about your events or accounts is sent. If www.tzurl.org cannot be reached, the phone's own data is used. Repeating events are still calculated from the phone's own data.

After a change, events already on the phone are checked and corrected at the next sync.
Time zone data is out of date

The time zone data on this phone is version %1$s and no longer seems to be updated. Events in places that have changed their clock rules since then can show at the wrong time.

Turn on "%2$s" to use current rules from www.tzurl.org instead. The app then sends requests to https://www.tzurl.org, which sees your IP address and the names of the time zones your events use, for example Europe/Berlin. Nothing else about your events or accounts is sent. Repeating events are still calculated from the phone's own data.

Proton creates a contact for everyone you exchange email with, and those have a display name and nothing else. Android will not store a name it cannot complete, so it splits one out of the display name: an address like app@example.com becomes the first name app@example and the surname com, and the name your phone then shows is app@example com, with the dot turned into a space.\n\nChoosing a field yourself leaves Android nothing to invent. Only contacts that have no first or last name on Proton are affected, and nothing is ever changed on Proton.
